mfg1-electrical-l078.title: Synchronous speed, mechanical output, and starting methods
mfg1-electrical-l078.objective: Read synchronous speed, actual speed, input, and shaft output separately.

paragraphs.title: Field speed and rotor speed
paragraphs.text: The rotating field’s synchronous speed for an AC induction machine is Ns=120 f/p. At 50 Hz and 4 poles it is 1500 min⁻¹, but a loaded induction rotor normally runs slower, with slip. Do not treat this expression as an unconditional guarantee of actual speed.

paragraphs.title: Calculate output from torque
paragraphs.text: Mechanical shaft output is P=2πNT/60, with actual speedN in min⁻¹ and torqueT in N·m. At 600 min⁻¹ and 2 N·m it is about 126 W. Distinguish input power from shaft output including losses; calculated output does not permit exceeding ratings.

paragraphs.title: Starting conditions
paragraphs.text: Full-voltage, star-delta, autotransformer, and reactor starting methods depend on use and installation. Star-delta current-reduction explanations assume suitable windings, connections, and other conditions. Do not rearrange terminals yourself; check starting current, load, and protection.

terms.meaning: Rotating-field speed determined by supply frequency and pole count.
A quantity expressing the difference between synchronous and induction-rotor speeds.
Mechanical output taken from a shaft.
Beginning operation from a stopped condition.

mfg1-electrical-l078.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Find synchronous speed at 60 Hz and 6 poles, and explain why a measured 980 min⁻¹is not the same. Calculate shaft output at 900 min⁻¹ and 4 N·m.
safety: Do not independently change motor terminals or phase order to test speed or direction.
mfg1-electrical-l078.summary: Read synchronous speed, actual speed, input, and shaft output separately.

mfg1-electrical-l079.title: Transformer losses, insulation construction, and the environment
mfg1-electrical-l079.objective: Distinguish losses from insulation construction, and observe protection, maintenance, and environmental conditions.

paragraphs.title: How losses grow
paragraphs.text: Core losses mainly occur in the core and exist when rated-condition voltage is applied to the primary even without secondary load. Copper loss is winding I²R; doubling current at unchanged resistance quadruples it. Stray load losses also exist, so the ideal ratio alone does not determine efficiency.

paragraphs.title: Insulation and cooling materials
paragraphs.text: Oil-filled, molded, and gas-insulated construction have different maintenance requirements. SF6 is an insulation-gas example with significant environmental impact; do not release it without authorization. Colorless and odorless does not mean safe; use equipment and material information.

paragraphs.title: Protection and the system
paragraphs.text: Check interrupting media and insulation against equipment specifications. Do not turn textbook overviews into claims that older technologies no longer exist at all; consult actual nameplates and procedures. Solar DC conversion and storage also belong to a system including connection and protection.

terms.meaning: Loss caused by winding resistance.
Loss occurring in the core.
Additional load losses associated with leakage flux and similar effects.
A construction in which resin or similar material solidifies insulation parts.

mfg1-electrical-l079.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Find the copper-loss ratio at 1.5 times current with unchanged winding resistance. Organize maintenance and environmental checks for oil, resin, and gas equipment.
safety: Do not drain insulation oil or gas, or open such equipment, without authorization.
mfg1-electrical-l079.summary: Distinguish losses from insulation construction, and observe protection, maintenance, and environmental conditions.

mfg1-electrical-l080.title: Inspection stages, reliability, and electrical safety
mfg1-electrical-l080.objective: Separate inspection stage and purpose, and use tests suited to equipment and conditions.

paragraphs.title: Components, assembled boards, and finished products
paragraphs.text: Incoming component checks, solder/orientation/electrical checks on assembled boards, and dimensional/function/appearance checks on completed products concern different targets. Supplier records do not authorize skipping your own required checks.

paragraphs.title: Environment and lifetime
paragraphs.text: Environmental tests apply defined temperature, humidity, vibration, or shock conditions. Reliability tests may use accelerated conditions to assess continued quality, but a single brief functional check cannot guarantee lifetime.

paragraphs.title: Safety and electromagnetic tests
paragraphs.text: Insulation resistance and withstand-voltage tests differ in purpose and method. Leakage and electromagnetic-immunity checks such as EMS may not be replaceable with an ordinary multimeter. Match test equipment, conditions, criteria, and personnel, and record results and the criteria used.

terms.meaning: A test examining operation or performance under specified environmental conditions.
The ability to retain required functions for the needed period.
A characteristic concerning insulation performance at a specified test voltage.
A concept concerning immunity to electromagnetic disturbance.

mfg1-electrical-l080.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Make an inspection record separating confirmed and unconfirmed requirements for a product with normal appearance but missing environmental tests. Explain why insulation-resistance and withstand-voltage tests are not the same.
safety: Do not independently add withstand-voltage or safety tests without approval.
mfg1-electrical-l080.summary: Separate inspection stage and purpose, and use tests suited to equipment and conditions.

mfg1-electrical-l081.title: Compare maintenance effects, terminology, and records
mfg1-electrical-l081.objective: Evaluate maintenance through what was done and the conditions of its effects.

paragraphs.title: Make the purpose specific
paragraphs.text: Maintenance aims for safety, fewer defects, longer life, and lower downtime losses and costs. Combine scheduled service, monitoring, and repair; do not always run cheap parts until failure.

paragraphs.title: Do not judge by terminology alone
paragraphs.text: The textbook narrowly distinguishes hozen and hoshu, but workplace and standard usage can include inspection and prevention within hoshu too. A name alone does not determine safety or responsibility; check actual work, stopping conditions, and restart criteria.

paragraphs.title: Conditions for comparing effects
paragraphs.text: Compare operating hours, production volume, repair contents, and downtime as well as failure counts. Shorter replacement intervals can prevent failure while increasing cost and waste. Predictive maintenance also needs monitoring equipment and control values.

terms.meaning: Maintenance performed beforehand to reduce failures.
Maintenance decisions based on condition-related warning signs.
Production and other losses caused by equipment stops.
A value defined for assessing a condition.

mfg1-electrical-l081.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Compare 2 failures in 100 operating hours with 3 in 300 hours as rates. Describe checks for maintenance method, cost, safety, and downtime losses.
safety: Do not omit isolation or authority checks even when the task is called routine inspection.
mfg1-electrical-l081.summary: Evaluate maintenance through what was done and the conditions of its effects.

mfg1-electrical-l082.title: Packaging marks, stacking, and PPM
mfg1-electrical-l082.objective: Apply marks to actual handling, and assess logistics quality using matching denominators.

paragraphs.title: Protection and distribution
paragraphs.text: Match packaging to shock, vibration, humidity, storage duration, and product shape. Cushioning and restraints have different roles. Select paper, cardboard, wood, metal, or resin for the purpose; the outer box’s appearance does not guarantee internal protection.

paragraphs.title: Apply handling marks
paragraphs.text: Distinguish fragile, keep dry, handle with care, do not stack, and stacking-count limits. In the textbook, n is the number allowed above the bottom package; verify actual labels and packaging specifications. Do not rewrite marks yourself to permit overloading.

paragraphs.title: Convert to parts per million
paragraphs.text: PPM expresses a count ratio per million.2 events in 10000 shipments is 2/10000×1000000=200 PPM. Do not fix acceptance values by industry or warehouse type alone; align customer target, population, period, and counting rules. Also assess timing, item, quantity, and destination.

terms.meaning: Expressing a proportion in parts per million.
A material reducing shock.
A material limiting product displacement.
An instruction limiting the number of stacked levels.

mfg1-electrical-l082.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Calculate PPM for 3 events in 25000 shipments. Draw different examples for do-not-stack and a limit of 2 above the bottom package. Make an assessment table including wrong destinations.
safety: Stack heavy packages only using specified handling methods and permitted conditions.
mfg1-electrical-l082.summary: Apply marks to actual handling, and assess logistics quality using matching denominators.

mfg1-electrical-l083.title: Injection molds, demolding, and FRP
mfg1-electrical-l083.objective: Separate flow paths, mold restraint, and removal; check composite properties against specifications.

paragraphs.title: The resin path
paragraphs.text: Injection molding feeds material from a hopper through a heated barrel and screw, then sprue, runner, and gate to the product cavity. Clamping holds the mold against injection pressure. Manage temperature, pressure, quantity, speed, and cooling under specified conditions.

paragraphs.title: Remove the shape and store safely
paragraphs.text: Draft angles aid removal, while ejector pins push out the product. Distinguish gates from sprues and check each product/mold design. Manage rust, humidity, and dirt in storage; do not share a different product’s mold without authorization.

paragraphs.title: Resin and fibers change properties
paragraphs.text: Thermoplastic, thermosetting, and biodegradable classifications differ in properties and treatment conditions. FRP’s mechanical and electrical behavior changes with glass/carbon fiber type, direction, and amount. Check strength, weight, chemical resistance, flammability, surface damage, disposal, and recycling against product specifications; not all FRP is identical.

terms.meaning: Separating and removing a molded product from its mold.
A slope helping a product release from the mold.
The entrance through which resin reaches the product cavity.
A pin used to push out a molded product.

mfg1-electrical-l083.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Diagram the roles of sprue, runner, gate, draft angle, and ejector. Explain why a carbon-fiber component cannot simply replace an insulating component.
safety: Do not put hands inside molds. Use isolated, approved procedures for clearing jams or changing molds.
mfg1-electrical-l083.summary: Separate flow paths, mold restraint, and removal; check composite properties against specifications.

mfg1-electrical-l084.title: Board structure, exposure, development, and etching
mfg1-electrical-l084.objective: Distinguish structure, pattern formation, and removal targets; protect needed copper with resist.

paragraphs.title: Layers and materials
paragraphs.text: Single-, double-, and multilayer describe conductive-layer structure; rigid, flexible, and combined types describe form. Paper phenolic, glass epoxy, ceramics, and metal bases differ in substrate and thermal conditions. A board with mounted components is at a different manufacturing stage.

paragraphs.title: Leave the needed conductors
paragraphs.text: Subtractive formation creates a protective pattern over copper foil and etches unwanted copper. Another method selectively plates conductors. Mask pattern, exposure, and development depend on resist type; do not apply the same light/dark conditions to every process.

paragraphs.title: Removing film and copper are different stages
paragraphs.text: The negative-resist concept here leaves exposed, hardened film, develops away unhardened film, etches exposed copper, then strips remaining protection. Do not describe needed protected copper as being removed along with it. Control temperature, concentration, cleaning, surface treatment, outline, and inspection conditions.

terms.meaning: Applying controlled light to photosensitive material.
Removing specified photosensitive-film portions after exposure to form a pattern.
Removing remaining film or similar material.
A wiring board combining multiple conductor layers.

mfg1-electrical-l084.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Color-code substrate, needed copper, unwanted copper, and resist. Explain the removal target in development, copper etching, and resist stripping. Explain why this concept is not an actual chemical recipe.
safety: Do not operate UV, chemicals, plating, or waste-liquid processes on the basis of textbook descriptions alone.
mfg1-electrical-l084.summary: Distinguish structure, pattern formation, and removal targets; protect needed copper with resist.
